newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish Postipankki sees smaller 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Finnish Postipankki sees smaller 1997 profit.

text.p: Finnish state-owned commercial bank Postipankki Oy said on Wednesday it expected to make a smaller profit this year than last due to tight interest margins and less income from securities trading.
"The group is expected to show a profit in 1997, although it will be smaller than in 1996," Postipankki said in a statement with its 1996 results.
The profit would fall "partly because low interest rates will maintain a narrow interest margin between lending and deposits", Postipankki said.
"Income from transactions on securities is unlikely to reach the same level as in 1996," it added.
In 1996, Postipankki's earnings improved robustly to a 602 million markka operating profit after credit losses from a 502 million loss the previous year.
CEO Eino Keinanen called the Postipankki group's performance in 1996 "satisfactory".
Competition in the banking sector would get tougher as European economic and monetary union was drawing closer. But Postipankki said it would remain competitive.

"Postipankki's standing in the provision of Finnish retail and corporate financial, investment and payment transactions services should not be threatened," it said, referring to its familiarity with the domestic financial markets.
